title: Detesting dressing up, avoiding church, listening to Sunday services
summary: Having dressed up so much in show business she dislikes hats and church clothes, so she stays home and listens to religious radio on Sundays.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: And then another thing, Chris, I had to dress up so much in show business. I had to spend so much money for clothes. And a lot of these girls that have these smart shops on Madison Avenue and in the different big stores, I got my clothes strictly from them. And then Patou dressed me in Paris, you know.
See? And I had to dress up so much that I detest clothes. I want to always be neat and passable.
Comfortable. And having to put on -- God knows I love him. I love God because he's been so good to

me. And still is. The reason -- one of the main reasons I don't go to church, I've got to put on a hat. I don't like hats. And I don't like -- I'll have to dress up a little to go to church. I don't want to wear my jeans to church, although people do wear jeans. But I don't want to put on jeans to go to church, so I stay away from church. And I have a little radio, and on WHN, tuned to WHN, and the only time I turn that radio on is say I start about 6:00 o'clock on Sunday morning, to listen to the services, and there's Dr. Oswald Hoffman comes on at 8:30, and I listen to him. But I leave that thing on from about, say about 6:00 o'clock, until all the religious services go off, and then I turn that radio off. I don't turn it on again until the next Sunday, at 6:00 o'clock, see, when I hear my services.
You don't even listen to music on the radio.
Well, I put my radio -- I have a Magnavox that I put on to listen to the news and other music.
But I leave that one on.
